text:
maya: Heads up — onboarding sample app is spamming logs when OTEL hooks are enabled. Lots of DEBUG from http-client, missing req_id in many lines, and redaction seems incomplete.

alex: Repro steps?

maya: Steps: checkout branch onboarding/otel-sample, run `./dev up --telemetry`. Log snippet below — note missing req_id and an email leaking in headers.

maya: ```
2026-03-23T12:03:01.123Z INFO server Starting service
2026-03-23T12:03:01.456Z DEBUG http-client request to /v1/generate
2026-03-23T12:03:01.457Z DEBUG http-client headers: Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED user_email=alice@example.com
2026-03-23T12:03:01.458Z WARN auth Missing req_id in request context
```

maya: Authorization token gets redacted but the user_email header is still in cleartext.

sam: Are you on the SDK pinned in sample app? We shipped a hook-ordering fix in 0.9.0 that changed when req_id is injected.

maya: The sample app has `redwood-sdk@0.8.2` in package.json. Also the dev script sets `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` for experimental telemetry ordering.

alex: That would explain it — otel_first means our OTEL hook runs before the logging injection hook, so logs emitted by http-client don't get req_id. For redaction, some headers are sanitized by the logging wrapper, but internal debug from node-fetch logs raw headers before wrapper sees them.

sam: Quick workaround: set `TELEMETY_HOOK_ORDER=logging_first` or upgrade SDK to ^0.9.0. Also we can add an extra sanitize pass in the http-client wrapper for any header values matching email regex.

maya: I tried `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=logging_first` and it reduced the missing req_id messages, but I still saw the email in a debug line coming from node-fetch internal debug output.

devex-bot: FYI — related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412 (hook ordering + header sanitization).

alex: Action plan: (1) Update sample app to ^0.9.0, (2) Add defensive header scrub in http-client wrapper, (3) Default onboarding env to `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info` so new users aren't overwhelmed by debug spam, (4) Add CI test that runs with `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` to ensure sanitization still holds.

sam: I'll open a PR for the sample app bump and the wrapper sanitization. I'll include a unit test that asserts no email-like substrings reach the logs when we simulate node-fetch debug output. Also I'll add a README blurb about `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER` and `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL`.

maya: Thanks — could you also add a small note in the onboarding quickstart: "If you see many DEBUG network logs, set REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info or upgrade the sample SDK". New users kept filing issues about this.

sam: Will do. Ping me if you want the PR to target the low-risk branch or main.

ci-bot: CI triggered for branch sam/telemetry-fix — tests: queued, build: queued. :gear:

maya: Awesome, thanks everyone :tada:

alex: Once PR is up, I'll review the sanitization and make sure we don't double-redact tokens (we only want to redact identifiers like emails and tokens, not useful sanitized IDs).

sam: Yep — will keep the scrub conservative.

maya: Closing the loop here — leaving the sample app in the dev environment until the PR lands so I can validate on my laptop.

alex: Thanks — appreciate the quick fix.
